admissionRule: observable can discriminate materially different live explanations
observable is not decision-equivalent to retained telemetry
collection does not silently assume the intervention being evaluated
result would change a research decision, reopen condition, or experiment design

opportunities.name: regime search-state / trajectory overlap
opportunities.observable: matched-context state/trajectory overlap and divergence locus between solver regimes

opportunities.name: heuristic rejection false-negative opportunity cost
opportunities.observable: independently justified continuation opportunity lost specifically at heuristic rejection/gating decisions

opportunities.name: mechanism interaction residual
opportunities.observable: matched-work A+B effect relative to an explicitly declared additive/null composition model, with gain/loss churn

opportunities.name: budget response / solve elasticity
opportunities.observable: solve/capability response across a prespecified bounded work ladder

opportunities.name: residual distance-to-solution / progress representation
opportunities.observable: a prespecified semantic/reference progress measure such as exact distance, witness decision distance, obligation deficit, remaining causal commitments, or calibrated completion headroom
distinguishes: superficial progress without viable completion basin
opportunities.canonicalPremiseAdmission: no; retain measurement opportunity until one representation proves decision-bearing

opportunities.name: cross-experiment gain/loss covariance and latent capability structure
opportunities.observable: ancestry-aware covariance/clustering of per-level or independent-unit gain/loss vectors across experiments

opportunities.name: research-process yield / premise fertility
opportunities.observable: decision-changing information gained per research effort, preserved as multiple diagnostics rather than one scalar score
distinguishes: capability acquisition with poor research attribution
opportunities.canonicalPremiseAdmission: no; research-process layer only unless a future decision rule earns semantic admission
